report:
The entire new continuation222 argument is sound relative to the four complete caller grants. Its exact conclusion is the finite-energy equation on the split projective line P^1_K over every complete characteristic-zero real-valued non-Archimedean field K, for every actual ample rational line bundle L, every continuous psh reference, and every positive Radon target of raw mass deg L satisfying the equivalent finite-dual/all-E1-integrability condition. Discreteness, algebraic closedness, residue characteristic zero, target invariance and skeletal support are unnecessary. Uniqueness concerns every actual E1 solution and holds at every analytic point as equality u=v+c, including common poles.

I checked each application of the complete O/D/N/T bodies. P^1 is smooth, geometrically integral and projective, and O(1) is an actual ample bundle, so O applies throughout. N establishes the standard reference atom, finite norming anchor, intrinsic criterion and decreasing-closure/energy facts used here. D supplies the completed-closure quotient, actual invariant singular descent, energy equality, unique invariant Radon lift and continuous-dual equality. T is applied only to trivially valued characteristic-zero fields. D's conditional equation transfer is used only after upstairs existence, equivariance and every-solution uniqueness have been established. Neither the original scope text nor the source ledger supplies an additional theorem.

The affine seminorm classification reconstructs without a restriction to C_v. Ultrametricity follows, if necessary, by expanding (f+h)^m and taking m-th roots of the bound (m+1)max(|f|,|h|)^m. For an attained minimum r=|T-a|, strong ultrametricity and minimality give |T-b|=max(r,|a-b|); factorization determines every polynomial norm. For a nonattained infimum, strictly decreasing r_j=|T-a_j| give nested closed disks. Their linear-polynomial norms squeeze to the original seminorm, and factorization gives convergence for every polynomial. A common point of the disks would attain the infimum. If their radii tended to zero, the centers would be Cauchy and completeness would produce such a common point. Thus empty chains have positive limiting radius and give exactly the type IV endpoints. Equal endpoint seminorms force mutual cofinality of the defining disk chains, so the construction is independent of their presentation.

The value-group argument is correct: one nonzero logarithmic value and all its rational multiples occur by taking roots, and that subgroup is dense in R. Multiplicativity of value-group-radius Gauss norms follows from reduction after scaling; continuity of the finite coefficient maximum then proves it for every positive radius. No spherical completeness or countability assumption enters.

The path and topology assertions also reconstruct. Comparable disks form radius-parametrized arcs, and two disks join at radius max(r,s,|a-b|). Empty-chain endpoints are obtained by adjoining the limiting end of their ancestor chain. Radius zero and the second coordinate chart give the classical endpoints and infinity. Polynomial evaluations are continuous along these arcs. Removing a positive-radius disk point separates its downward open-disk directions from its exterior direction; these sets are expressed by strict linear-polynomial inequalities. Every path between separated points must cross that disk point. Such separating points determine the constructed arc, proving uniqueness. Factorization makes linear-polynomial evaluations sufficient for the affine analytic topology. On each finite tree, the compact metric realization maps continuously and injectively into the Hausdorff analytic carrier, hence has precisely its induced topology. This does not identify the full analytic topology with the global path-metric topology. The omitted essential arguments in the [AWS notes](https://swc-math.github.io/aws/2007/BakerNotesMarch21.pdf) were therefore reconstructed, rather than imported as proved assertions. The literal [Baker–Rumely version 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0407433v1) retains its C_v analytic scope; its complete finite-graph Sections 3.2–3.3 are only a compatible check of the elementary tree calculation. Its logarithmic normalization is not substituted for the manuscript's natural logarithm.

The normalized FS kernel is correct in every configuration. For x=ζ(b,s), y=ζ(a,r), set S=max(1,|b|,s), R=max(1,|a|,r), and M=max(r,s,|a-b|). Direct evaluation gives u_y(x)=log M−log S−log R. The root distances are 2log S−log s and 2log R−log r, and the distance between the disks is 2log M−log s−log r. Their common-root length is therefore log S+log R−log M, exactly −u_y(x). This includes disks inside the unit disk, disks containing it, and disks centered outside it. At infinity, u_y(∞)=−log R. Classical and type IV endpoint values follow from the same evaluations and their ancestor limits.

The new model application meets the precise hypotheses of external premise 0. When r=|c|, the generic coordinate is w=(T−a)/c. Its Gauss point evaluates T−b as max(|a−b|,|c|), so the unique Shilov point of the reduced standard model is exactly ζ(a,r). The only special-fiber component is P^1 over the residue field, and the restricted O(1) has degree one. Thus the genuine curvature atom has coefficient one. I read the complete [BE Example 8.11 and formula (8.3)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3), and the pertinent complete proof units [CLD 6.9.2–6.9.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v1), including the algebraically closed coefficient proof and its calibration lemma. No residue-characteristic assumption or discretely valued model theorem is being extended. For arbitrary positive r, replacing r by value-group radii gives uniform convergence of the FS scalars: the numerator error is bounded by |log r_j−log r|, and the normalization has the same continuity. The disk points converge analytically, so genuine uniform-to-weak continuity proves MA(u_y)=δ_y.

For each finite rooted tree, its finite-leaf kernel coordinates separate its points. Their compact embedding and the identities g(r_Γx,y)=g(x,y) establish analytic continuity of the retraction. The common-path kernel is symmetric, bounded on Γ² and jointly continuous; changing its second argument changes it by at most the path distance. Consequently g_Γ is bounded and jointly continuous on the entire product carrier. Projected targets are positive Radon probabilities, including diffuse ones. Finite Borel partitions of small metric diameter approximate their kernel integrals uniformly by convex sums. Positive real convexity and uniform closure on the fixed bundle are supplied by the grants. Affine curvature dependence, followed by uniform operator continuity, proves the genuine identity MA(u_Γ)=μ_Γ; the operator is never defined by assigning that target.

The weak-convergence proof works for the entire directed family. Distinct points are separated by a finite positive-radius disk kernel on an appropriate root branch, including comparable points and terminal endpoints. Constants and these kernels generate a separating real algebra on the compact Hausdorff carrier. The Stone–Weierstrass application has exactly those hypotheses. Its elementary density argument can also be reconstructed here: the uniform closure is a lattice because polynomial approximations to absolute value give finite maxima and minima; two-point interpolation and two finite compact covers then approximate any continuous function. Thus no metrizability is needed. Each algebra element uses finitely many disk kernels and is fixed by every retraction containing their points. If it approximates a continuous test within ε, the test's projected and original integrals differ by at most 2ε on that tail. Hence μ_Γ converges weakly to μ without a cofinal sequence.

The monotonicity and energy bounds have the correct directions and factors. Writing d_Γ(x) for the retained root length, g_Γ(x,z)=min(g(x,z),d_Γ(x),d_Γ(z)); inclusion increases this kernel and decreases u_Γ. All potentials remain anchored at ξ with value zero. Decreasing closure gives an actual psh endpoint, and the anchor excludes the identically −∞ function. Fubini is applied only to bounded continuous projected kernels. Retraction invariance identifies both relevant integrals with −I_Γ, while the reference integral is zero. Therefore E(u_Γ)=−I_Γ/2 and the dual objective is I_Γ/2. Finite J bounds every I_Γ by 2J. Decreasing energy continuity, which allows a possibly infinite endpoint energy before this bound is used, establishes E(u)>−∞. Only then is O applied to infer MA(u)=μ from the actual decreasing continuous net. There is no completion-to-potential realization assumption.

The singular symmetry identity follows from the exact granted polynomial and derivative. With A=∫p MA(p), B=∫p MA(q), C=∫q MA(p), the derivative of the expanded curve energy at zero is −A+(B+C)/2. O's segment derivative is C−A, so B=C. All these integrals are finite by O. Taking q=u_y then determines p(y)=−∫g(z,y)dμ(z) for every finite positive-radius disk point; O also establishes finiteness of p at that point.

Terminal recovery is valid for every actual solution. A homogeneous section factors into linear forms over C. Each linear form's relative log norm is its Gauss log norm minus its common-root kernel with its zero; the infinity zero is checked in the second chart. These kernels increase along outward root paths, so section log norms, weighted FS maxima and their actual decreasing endpoints are radially nonincreasing. For ordered disk ancestors approaching a terminal x, p(y_i) decreases to ℓ≥p(x). Extended-valued upper semicontinuity gives p(x)≥ℓ. Hence p(x)=ℓ, including a literal −∞ limit. This determines every terminal value and proves all-point uniqueness without subtracting infinite values.

Concavity and the initial segment derivative give E(v)−E(u)≤∫(v−u)dμ for every actual E1 competitor, proving maximization. O's weighted continuity applies with the curvature potential fixed at u and decreasing continuous majorants as weights. It identifies the continuous-test supremum with the actual maximizer's value. Applied to the constructed net, it proves J(μ)=sup_Γ I_Γ/2, E(u)=−sup_Γ I_Γ/2 and ∫u dμ=−sup_Γ I_Γ. These quantities are finite under the target condition. These kernel formulas concern the standard anchored reference in the nontrivially valued algebraically closed construction.

The completed-closure application has all its antecedents. Algebraic closedness of the completion can independently be checked by approximating a monic polynomial by monic polynomials over the algebraic closure. Their roots have a common bound. Factorization lets one choose successive roots at distances tending to zero, using the small value of the next polynomial at the previous root. Ultrametric completeness gives a root of the limiting polynomial, and repeated division gives splitting. Thus the upstairs field has exactly the domain required by the tree proof. Semilinear transformations transport FS systems, preserve the invariant reference and continuous energy, and commute with the continuous operator by D. Decreasing energy continuity and O's defining operator limits extend these statements to actual E1 potentials. The normalized upstairs solution therefore solves the same invariant target after every transformation; established all-point uniqueness makes it invariant. D descends the actual singular metric and its energy, and O pushes its genuine measure to μ with unchanged mass. For any downstairs solution, its upstairs measure is invariant and pushes to μ; D's unique invariant lift identifies that measure with the same upstairs target. Upstairs uniqueness and quotient surjectivity then prove equality at every downstairs point. No singular averaging or transport of arbitrary noninvariant singular tests is used. Maximization downstairs also follows directly from O's concavity and derivative once the downstairs solution exists.

The rational-bundle extension is correct. A generic trivialization on the smooth curve gives a divisor. An affine irreducible polynomial of degree d has divisor [closed point]−d[∞], and rational-function factorization shows every principal divisor has degree zero. This proves Pic(P^1_K)=Z and identifies every actual ample rational bundle with O(a), a∈Q_{>0}. Clearing denominators in section systems gives the exact actual cone correspondence u=av. Continuous curvature and energy yield MA_a(av)=a MA_1(v) and E_a(av)=a²E_1(v); corresponding continuous majorants and O's decreasing continuity extend these identities to singular endpoints. For μ=aν, J_a(μ)=a²J_1(ν). Thus the operator and raw mass scale by a, whereas energy and dual scale by a². For a new reference differing by b, the cocycle gives J_new(μ)=J_old(μ)−E_old(b)+∫b dμ. This correction is finite, and the absolute equation, intrinsic condition, maximization and uniqueness are unchanged.

Harmless reader clarifications: throughout the tree sections, Z denotes (P^1_C)^an; “finite disk point” means positive finite radius, excluding classical radius-zero points; terminal ancestors are directed outward toward the endpoint. BE's internal pointer to CLD 6.9.2 identifies support, while coefficients are justified by 6.9.3–6.9.4 and 6.9.6. The final reference to the remaining positive-residue-characteristic axis concerns its general geometric scope: the proved P^1 sector itself includes positive residue characteristic. None of these clarifications changes the argument or requires a substantial repair.

Original P16.4 remains open outside the proved sector and the granted trivial-field theorem. In particular, no nontrivially valued higher-genus or general-variety equation, nonsplit genus-zero equation, or general envelope/compactness/comparison replacement is established here. O already grants the all-field E1 operator; the remaining general equation inputs are not supplied by this kernel construction. The separate singular, nonample, nonprojective and nonalgebraizable axes are not closed. Compilation, historical review labels and provenance hashes were not used as mathematical evidence. The audit was read-only, with no protected-editor changes or campaign feedback.

passages.statement: Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued real-valued non-Archimedean field C, let (𝓧,𝓛) be a projective model of a smooth geometrically integral projective curve X/C, with reduced special fiber, and let φ𝓛 be its continuous model metric. Each irreducible special-fiber component Y determines a unique Shilov point xY, and the genuine continuous curvature measure is dd^cφ𝓛 = ΣY deg(𝓛|Y) δxY. The formula also applies to rational model line bundles with rational intersection degrees. The value-group factor is one, without a discreteness or residue-characteristic-zero hypothesis. See Boucksom–Eriksson arXiv:1805.01016v3, Example 8.11 and (8.3), and Chambert-Loir–Ducros arXiv:1204.6277v1, 6.9.2–6.9.6.
